title: Integral Verdier biduality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work on the small pro-etale site with the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_X=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)=D(\widehat R_X)$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the derived-complete integral category $D^b_c(X,R)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and its uniform finite-Tor subcategory $D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], and let $\operatorname{Res}_n$ be derived restriction of scalars [def-weil-integral-derived-restriction-of-scalars].

Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism and let $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_{X,n}^!A_n$ be its finite pro-etale dualizing object at coefficient level $n$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and let $\omega_{X,R}$ be the derived-complete integral dualizing object with its reductions $\omega_{X,R}\otimes_R^L A_n\cong\omega_{X,n}$ [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Set
$$
D_{X,R}K=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,\omega_{X,R}),\qquad
D_{X,n}M=R\mathcal Hom_{(A_n)_X}(M,\omega_{X,n}),
$$
using the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then $D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$, and $D_{X,R}$ restricts to an exact contravariant anti-equivalence of this category. For every $K$ in it the canonical evaluation-defined reduction comparisons are isomorphisms, and the output is reconstructed from those reductions:
$$
(D_{X,R}K)\otimes_R^L A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,n}K_n,
\qquad
D_{X,R}K\cong R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Res}_nD_{X,n}K_n.
$$
Here $\otimes_R^L A_n$ means the displayed derived reduction over $\widehat R_X$. The second formula means the derived-completeness Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-complete], with reduction maps to the finite duals identified by the first comparisons and transition maps induced by finite evaluation and the dualizing reduction maps. In accordance with [def-weil-derived-limit], it asserts reconstruction as a derived limit; it does not specify an isomorphism to an independently chosen model of that limit.

For an integer $d\geq0$, if $\dim X\leq d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and all $K_n$ have Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ for integers $a\leq b$, all reductions of $D_{X,R}K$ have Tor amplitude in $[-b-2d,-a]$. The first comparisons preserve evaluation and its transposes. In particular they identify the reduction of the actual evaluation-defined double-dual map
$$
\delta_K:K\longrightarrow D_{X,R}D_{X,R}K
$$
with the finite double-dual map $\delta_{K_n}$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. The map $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism, natural in $K$.

proof.text: Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$. Its residue reduction $K_1$ is bounded by the definition of this category, so choose integers $a\leq b$ containing its cohomological support. Lemma [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] gives Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for every $K_n$, not just boundedness separately at each level. Thus every object of $D^b_c(X,R)$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]; the reverse inclusion is the definition of that full subcategory. For subsequent uniform bounds choose $d\geq0$ with $\dim X\leq d$, possible by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; the empty scheme allows $d=0$.

Put $H=R\mathcal Hom_{\widehat R_X}(K,\omega_{X,R})$. The object $\omega_{X,R}$ is derived complete and its reductions are $\omega_{X,n}$ by [prop-coef-integral-dualizing]. Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] with $L=\omega_{X,R}$. It says that $H$ is derived complete and that the actual evaluation-defined comparison identifies $H_n$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(K_n,\omega_{X,n})=D_{X,n}K_n$. In particular this is a property of the ambient internal Hom, with no assumption that $K$ is site-perfect.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: the dualizing object and internal-Hom reduction

proof.text: For each $n$, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies a bounded constructible etale complex $K'_n$ with $\nu_X^*K'_n\cong K_n$. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii), $K'_n$ has the same Tor interval $[a,b]$ as $K_n$. Apply [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] on the etale site: $D_{X,\mathrm{et}}K'_n$ is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude $[-b-2d,-a]$, independent of $n$. The same preservation theorem applied to the constant rank-one input gives bounded constructibility of the etale dualizing object, since $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}((A_n)_X,\omega)=\omega$; the input is constructible and Tor concentrated in degree zero. Thus the second variable required by [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] is bounded constructible. Its internal-Hom and dualizing-object comparisons identify the pullback with $D_{X,n}K_n$. Clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] therefore gives constructibility and the same Tor bound on the pro-etale site. By step 2 these are the reductions of $H$. Taking the degree-zero module sheaf $(A_n)_X$ in the definition of Tor amplitude shows that their cohomology is in this one interval. Together with completeness, these facts are precisely [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so $H\in D^b_c(X,R)$. The argument works for any uniform input interval $[a,b]$, proving the stated quantitative bound.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite preservation and uniform interval

proof.text: Use the reduction tower with its actual maps defined in [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Since $H$ is derived complete, [def-weil-derived-complete] gives a distinguished triangle $H\to\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nH_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n\operatorname{Res}_nH_n\to H[1]$, whose first map has the actual reduction maps as components. Put $F_n=D_{X,n}K_n$ and write $b_n:\operatorname{Res}_nH_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_nF_n$ for the comparisons of step 2 after restriction of scalars. The finite-dual transition $u_n:\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_nF_n$ is adjoint to finite evaluation followed by the dualizing transition $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}\omega_{X,n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_{X,n}$, after reducing the input. The evaluation/transposition compatibility of [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] says that $u_n b_{n+1}$ and $b_n t_n^H$ have that same transpose, so $u_n b_{n+1}=b_n t_n^H$, or explicitly $u_n=b_n t_n^H b_{n+1}^{-1}$, in the single ambient category $D(\widehat R_X)$. Hence $B=\prod_n b_n$ satisfies $(1-s_F)B=B(1-s_H)$, as is checked on the $n$-th projection by this equation. Replacing the two product vertices by $B$ gives a distinguished Roos triangle for $H$ and $(\operatorname{Res}_nF_n,u_n)$; its first arrow has components $b_nc_n^H$. This is precisely reconstruction in [def-weil-derived-limit]. No interchange of cohomology with an ordinary limit is used.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: reconstruction from completeness

proof.text: Take the small skeleton supplied by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in its fixed larger universe. Internal Hom on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat R_X)$ is contravariantly exact in its first variable by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Its restriction to $D^b_c(X,R)$ is exact because step 3 proves preservation and [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] supplies the inherited triangulated structure. Define $\mathrm{ev}_K:DK\otimes^L K\to\omega_{X,R}$ to be evaluation and define $\delta_K$ as the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_K$ with the two factors interchanged. This tensor-Hom adjunction is available for this ring sheaf: combine the currying isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] with [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], which identifies degree-zero global Hom with derived-category morphisms. Write $\sigma_{P,Q}:P\otimes^LQ\to Q\otimes^LP$ for tensor symmetry. On K-flat models it is the sheaf tensor symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] multiplied by $(-1)^{ij}$ on the summand $P^i\otimes Q^j$; substitution in the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] verifies that it is a chain map and that $\sigma_{Q,P}\sigma_{P,Q}=1$. The defining transpose equation is $\mathrm{ev}_{DK}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1_{DK})=\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,DK}$. For $u:K\to L$, the transposes of $D^2(u)\delta_K$ and $\delta_Lu$ both equal $\mathrm{ev}_K\circ(Du\otimes1_K)\circ\sigma_{K,DL}$, by naturality of evaluation. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore proves $D^2(u)\delta_K=\delta_Lu$. Thus this is the actual ambient double-dual transformation.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the evaluation-defined double dual; exactness made explicit

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction] first to $K,\omega_{X,R}$ and then to $DK,\omega_{X,R}$; step 3 ensures that $DK$ is again in the integral category. The two comparisons identify $(D^2K)_n$ with $D_{X,n}^2K_n$. Because they preserve evaluation and transposes, they carry the reduction of the transpose defining $\delta_K$ to the transpose of finite evaluation, namely $\delta_{K_n}$ as specified in [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. By [thm-fix-general-biduality] this finite map is an isomorphism on the pro-etale site: step 1 already checked the required constructibility and finite Tor amplitude. This identifies a specified map, rather than merely producing an unspecified isomorphism between the same objects.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: reduction of the actual double-dual map

proof.text: Take a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{\delta_K}D^2K\to C\to K[1]$. Since the first two objects lie in $D^b_c(X,R)$, [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] (with shifts/rotation) puts $C$ there; in particular $C$ is derived complete. Derived reduction is exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], applied to $\widehat R_X\to(A_n)_X$. By step 6 and [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero], every $C_n$ is zero. In the Roos triangle for $C$ from [def-weil-derived-complete], both products are consequently zero objects. Apply [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] to its rotation $0\to0\to C[1]\to0$: the arrow $0\to0$ is an isomorphism, hence $C[1]$ and $C$ are zero. Apply the same cone criterion to the original triangle to conclude that $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism. This uses completeness of the cone, not a Nakayama assertion for a different integral coefficient category.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the derived-complete cone is zero

proof.text:
Use the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], with the symmetry of step 5 [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Suppressing the subscript $X,R$, uncurrying $D(\delta_K)\circ\delta_{DK}$ gives the following maps $DK\otimes^L K\to\omega_{X,R}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ev}_K\circ((D\delta_K\circ\delta_{DK})\otimes1_K)
&=\mathrm{ev}_{D^2K}\circ(\delta_{DK}\otimes\delta_K)\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_{DK}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1_{DK})\circ\sigma_{DK,K}\\
&=\mathrm{ev}_K.
\end{aligned}
$$
The first equality is evaluation naturality for $\delta_K$; the second is the defining transpose equation for $\delta_{DK}$ and naturality of $\sigma$; the third is the defining equation for $\delta_K$ and $\sigma_{K,DK}\sigma_{DK,K}=1$. Since the identity of $DK$ also uncurries to $\mathrm{ev}_K$, injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $D(\delta_K)\circ\delta_{DK}=1_{DK}$. All $\delta_K$ are invertible by step 7, so $D\delta_K=\delta_{DK}^{-1}$. For $u:K\to L$, naturality gives $u=\delta_L^{-1}\circ D(Du)\circ\delta_K$, proving injectivity on morphisms. For $v:DL\to DK$ set $u=\delta_L^{-1}\circ Dv\circ\delta_K$. Naturality at $v$ states $D^2v\circ\delta_{DL}=\delta_{DK}\circ v$, and hence
$$
Du=D\delta_K\circ D^2v\circ D(\delta_L^{-1})
=\delta_{DK}^{-1}\circ D^2v\circ\delta_{DL}=v.
$$
This proves full faithfulness. For every $L$, the isomorphism $\delta_L:L\xrightarrow{\sim}D(DL)$ exhibits $L$ as an object of the essential image, since $DL$ is in the category by step 3. Together with exactness from step 5 this proves the exact anti-equivalence and its natural biduality.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: evaluation identity and anti-equivalence

split_report.summary: Second reading made the structure morphism and integer dimension bound explicit, wrote the transition square and product conjugation, and expanded the signed evaluation and full-faithfulness calculations. Made the implicit finite-field/DVR/pro-etale/completed-ring hypotheses explicit, typed all reductions, and interpreted reconstruction by the existing Roos definition rather than a canonical isomorphism to an unspecified limit model. Expanded the two imported paragraphs into eight steps: uniform residue Tor bounds, actual Hom reduction, explicit etale-origin and Tor transport, reconstruction, ringed-site exactness/evaluation, finite biduality of the specified map, complete-cone conservativity, and the elementary anti-equivalence argument. No new nodes; all non-elementary tools are existing statements.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-4 realize the first proof paragraph; steps 5-8 realize the second. This is the integral coefficient transport prescribed by sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, not a replacement route. The unit has no proof steps and its realized statement list already includes this item, so no unit record is changed.

tool_uses.why: General ringed-site internal-Hom currying and exactness, applied to the completed coefficient sheaf. The etale-only lem-sf-hom-triangulated does not cover that ringed site.
Generic finite-dimensionality of a finite-type scheme over a field supplies a single dimension bound; the unit has no such dimension lemma.
Generic finite-coefficient etale-origin equivalence supplies K prime at each level before the etale preservation theorem is applied; the unit has no other origin statement.
Generic ringed-site identification of degree-zero global internal Hom with morphisms, used for the evaluation adjunction; it proves no geometric or integral duality.
Generic symmetry of tensor on modules over any sheaf of rings supplies the symmetry used in transposing evaluation; it proves no duality theorem.
